description: Composite of four secondary-electron SEM micrographs comparing the surface corrosion morphology of low-density steels after potentiodynamic polarization; each panel carries a white label box (a)-(d) in its top-left corner. (a) S0 (50 µm scale bar) shows a broad, largely smooth surface scattered with numerous small circular pits plus one larger, darker pit with a bright corrosion-product rim at lower right. (b) S950 (50 µm scale bar) is almost featureless except a single small pit circled by a yellow dashed line and labelled "pitting". (c) S1050 (100 µm scale bar) shows three isolated corrosion pits indicated by orange arrows with the label "pitting"; a green solid box marks one pit and connects by a dashed green line to a magnified inset (10 µm scale bar) showing a dark, irregular pit with a bright halo. (d) S1150 (50 µm scale bar) displays a single clearly larger, dark crater-like pit with a bright rim, annotated "pitting" (orange arrow) and "pitting corrosion expansion" (green text). The sequence demonstrates that pit number and size are greatest for S0, smallest for S950, and increase again for S1050 and S1150.

observations.observation: The figure comprises four SEM micrographs arranged in a 2x2 grid, labelled (a)-(d) in white boxes at the top-left of each panel.
Panel (a), S0, has a 50 µm scale bar and shows a surface densely covered with small circular pits together with one markedly larger dark pit enclosed by a bright rim.
Panel (b), S950, has a 50 µm scale bar and is almost free of features apart from one small pit highlighted by a yellow dashed circle with the label 'pitting'.

Panel (c), S1050, has a 100 µm scale bar (different magnification from the other panels) and shows three pits marked by orange arrows with the label 'pitting'; a green box and dashed green leader line connect one pit to a magnified inset with a 10 µm scale bar.
Panel (d), S1150, has a 50 µm scale bar and shows a single large dark pit with a bright rim annotated 'pitting' (orange) and 'pitting corrosion expansion' (green).
The caption assigns the panels as (a) S0, (b) S950, (c) S1050 and (d) S1150, i.e. the low-density steels after different solution-treatment temperatures.
The citing text states the corrosion morphology was produced after potentiodynamic polarization to 5 mA/cm2.
The citing text attributes the extensive corrosion damage and numerous deep pits of S0 (Fig. 7a) to elevated surface residual stress and a heterogeneous grain-boundary distribution.
The citing text reports that after solution treatment at 950 °C (S950, Fig. 7b) the steel shows only slight pitting with smaller pit sizes, indicating superior corrosion resistance.
The citing text reports that with increasing grain size the S1050 and S1150 samples show more and larger corrosion pits, corrosion expansion on some pit walls, and decreased corrosion resistance.
Pit size increases in the order S950 < S0/S1050 < S1150 as judged from the annotated pits, although the differing scale bars (50 µm vs 100 µm in (c)) mean panels are not at identical magnification.
No numeric pit depth, diameter or corrosion-rate values are printed on any panel; only textual labels ('pitting', 'pitting corrosion expansion') and scale bars are given.

subfigures.description: SEM surface of S0 after polarization; 50 µm scale bar. Many small circular pits plus one larger dark pit with bright rim at lower right; overall extensive pitting.
SEM surface of S950; 50 µm scale bar. Nearly clean surface with a single small pit circled by a yellow dashed line and annotated 'pitting'.

SEM surface of S1050; 100 µm scale bar. Three isolated pits arrowed in orange and labelled 'pitting'; one pit boxed in green and magnified in an inset (10 µm scale bar) showing a dark irregular pit with a bright halo.
SEM surface of S1150; 50 µm scale bar. One large dark crater-like pit with bright rim, annotated 'pitting' (orange arrow) and 'pitting corrosion expansion' (green text).
